issues.legal_issue: A tribunal hearing a statutory appeal must decide it on its merits and record its decision even when the appellant does not appear.
material_facts: The appellants brought statutory appeals against compensation awards.
The tribunal dismissed the appeals because the appellants’ advocate did not appear, without deciding the merits.
issues.conclusion: The tribunal had no power to dismiss the appeals for non-prosecution; it was required to decide them on their merits and record its decision despite the appellants’ default.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 17(1) and 20 of the Bombay Merged Territories and Areas (Jagirs Abolition) Act, 1953, the tribunal must decide an appeal and record its decision, and that decision is final and conclusive. Dismissal for want of prosecution is not a decision of the appeal within section 17(1). The court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: statutory_appeal and merits_decision_required and appeal_decision_final and appellant_absent

predicates.statutory_appeal: A party has brought an appeal to a tribunal under a statutory compensation scheme.
predicates.merits_decision_required: The governing law requires the tribunal to decide the appeal and record its decision.
predicates.appeal_decision_final: The governing law makes the tribunal’s decision on appeal final and conclusive.
predicates.appellant_absent: The appellant does not appear when the appeal is called for hearing.

issues.definition: When a statutory compensation appeal is subject to a duty to decide and record a final decision, the tribunal must decide it on its merits even if the appellant is absent.

issues.legal_issue: The restoration procedure and its receipt-based filing deadline apply to an appeal dismissed for non-appearance.
material_facts: The tribunal dismissed the appellants’ appeals for non-prosecution.
The appellants sought restoration after receiving the dismissal orders and filed their applications within thirty days of receipt.
The tribunal calculated the filing period from the dates of the dismissal orders and rejected the applications as late.
issues.conclusion: The restoration procedure covered appeals dismissed for non-prosecution, and the applications were timely because they were filed within thirty days of receipt of the dismissal orders.
issues.legal_principle: Regulations 20 and 21 of the Bombay Revenue Tribunal Regulations, 1958, apply to restoration applications following an appeal decided ex parte, including an appeal dismissed for non-prosecution under Regulation 19(1). Regulation 21 measures the filing period from receipt of the dismissal order. Regulation 55 provides for use of the Code of Civil Procedure only on matters not provided for in the Regulations. The court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.appeal_restoration_proceeding: A party seeks restoration of an appeal that was dismissed after the party did not appear.
predicates.appeal_dismissed_for_nonappearance: The tribunal dismissed the appeal because the appellant did not appear.
predicates.restoration_procedure_covers_ex_parte_di: The governing restoration procedure includes ex parte appeals dismissed for non-appearance.
predicates.application_filed_within_receipt_based_d: The restoration application was filed within the applicable filing period measured from receipt of the dismissal order.

issues.definition: A restoration application is timely when it follows an appeal dismissed for non-appearance, the restoration procedure covers that kind of ex parte dismissal, and the application is filed within the period measured from receipt of the dismissal order.
